author: historian-agent:o-s10
title: Battle of Santa Clara, December 1958
summary: In late December 1958 Che Guevara's column of about 300 rebels attacked Santa Clara, defended by a garrison of roughly 3,500 soldiers. His men derailed an armoured train with a bulldozer and forced its troops out; the train surrendered at 7 pm on 30 December. The city's fall dealt a decisive blow to Batista, who fled within hours.

as_recorded.value: the armoured train surrendered at 7pm on 30 December 1958

where.modern_name: Santa Clara, Villa Clara Province, Cuba
where.historical_name: Santa Clara, Las Villas Province, Republic of Cuba

importance.justification: Decisive rebel victory of the Cuban Revolution; Batista left the island within hours of the city falling.

related.because: The rebellion that ended at Santa Clara was fought against the military regime Batista installed in 1952.

beats.caption: About 300 guerrillas under Che Guevara faced a garrison of roughly 3,500 in Santa Clara and derailed the armoured train by removing track.
Molotov cocktails forced the train's soldiers out, and it surrendered at 7 pm.
Batista fled the island within twelve hours of the city being captured, and the captured weapons strengthened Castro's forces.

sources.title: CubaSi: A revolutionary train of thought

reviewer_note: Start of the fighting (often given as 28 December) was not on an opened page, so the date is 'late December 1958'. Both sources are secondary; the Cuba Solidarity Campaign article is an advocacy publication. Beat dated 1958-12-31 is placed by the 'within 12 hours' wording relative to the 30 December surrender and the capture; the exact capture day was not confirmed on an opened page. Garrison size and rebel numbers are given as the source states them.
